_source: 酷讯 Unified Session Structure - drill set for the 30/30/30 session (Warm-up routine + games, Skills block, Constrained game block)

_instructions.import: Hoopwise > Drill Library > Import. Drills already present by name are skipped by the app's dedupe step.
_instructions.tags: Search the library for unified-structure, block-warmup, block-skills or block-game to filter by session block.

drills.name: Full Court Dribble Progression
drills.description: Routine opener of the unified session. Every player has a ball and travels baseline to baseline, one dribble type per trip, in the same order every session so the moves become automatic.
instructions: Each player takes a ball and lines up on the baseline in 2-4 lines
Trip 1: regular dribble, right hand down, left hand back
Trip 2: skip dribble, one bounce per skip, switch hands on the way back
Trip 3: in-and-out dribble, fake the crossover and keep the ball in the same hand
Trip 4: alternate dribble, crossover on every bounce, left to right to left
Add the age-group moves: between the legs, behind the back, retreat dribble, hesitation
Once the group is ready, finish the last trips with a layup at the far basket
keyPoints: Eyes up, never on the ball
Fingertips, not the palm
Dribble below the waist with knees bent
Same order every session so the routine becomes second nature
Coach walks the lines and corrects one player at a time
variations: U6/U8: walking speed; on the whistle jump stop into triple threat
U10+: add between the legs and behind the back
U12+: add change of pace (slow to fast) and the retreat dribble
Race format: the last two trips are relays against another line

drills.name: Layup Progression
drills.description: Routine finishing ladder of the unified session, run basket to basket. Progresses from footwork without a dribble to finishing against obstacles.
instructions: Step 1: no dribble, carry the ball high in the shooting hand with the arm extended, run full court and finish a layup
Step 2: no dribble, run full court moving the ball around the waist, then finish a layup
Step 3: dribble basket to basket and finish a layup, right side with the right hand
Step 4: same on the left side with the left hand
Step 5: add obstacles, cones or chairs to weave around before the finish
Step 6: add a passive defender standing in the lane, then a live chasing defender
keyPoints: Outside hand shoots, inside foot jumps: right hand off the left foot
Knee drives up on the shooting side
Ball goes up high with a soft touch off the glass
Run through the layup, no slowing down at the rim
Both hands every session, the weak side gets equal reps
variations: U6: lower rim, coach hands the ball at the elbow of the lane
U8/U10: add the reverse layup and the opposite hand finish
U12+: euro step, floater, power layup through contact
Timed team challenge: total makes in 2 minutes

drills.name: Shooting Routine Ladder
drills.description: Routine shooting block that closes the warm-up routine. Short and identical every session, built from close-range form shooting up to the game spots of the age group.
instructions: Rung 1: one-hand form shooting from 1 meter, 5 makes on each side of the rim
Rung 2: two-hand form shooting from the block, 5 makes on each side
Rung 3: three spots (left elbow, free throw line, right elbow), 3 makes each, partner rebounds
Rung 4 (U10+): catch and shoot from a partner pass with 1-2 step footwork
Rung 5 (U12+): one-dribble pull-up from each spot
keyPoints: Elbow under the ball, wrist snapped, hold the follow-through
Feet set before the catch
Legs give the power, arms give the direction
Count makes, not attempts
Partner rebounds and returns a chest or bounce pass
variations: U6: shoot at a lowered rim or into a hoop held by the coach
Competition: first pair to 15 makes
Pressure: miss two in a row and restart the rung

drills.name: Pass and Tag
drills.description: Warm-up chase game with one ball. Taggers can only tag while holding the ball and cannot move with it, so they must pass to hunt. Develops passing speed, court vision and communication.
instructions: Mark a playing area, half court for 8-10 players
Two taggers share one ball, everyone else is a runner
The tagger holding the ball may pivot but not run or dribble
Taggers pass to each other to get close to a runner and tag by touching with the ball held in both hands, no throwing at runners
A tagged runner joins the taggers
Last runner standing wins, restart with two new taggers
keyPoints: Taggers must talk and call names before passing
Runners read the ball and move away from the receiver's side
Pass to where the teammate will be, not where they are
Coach shrinks the area if runners escape too easily
variations: U6: taggers may take two steps with the ball
Two balls once there are five or more taggers
U10+: runners must dribble a ball while escaping

drills.name: Police and Thieves
drills.description: Dribble tag game. Thieves dribble inside the area while the police try to knock the ball away. Teaches dribbling under pressure with the eyes up.
instructions: Half court, every thief has a ball, one or two police without a ball
Thieves dribble continuously, a thief who stops dribbling or steps out is caught
Police catch a thief by knocking the ball away or touching it
Caught thieves go to jail at the free throw line and do 10 crossovers
A free thief can release a jailed teammate with a high five while still dribbling
Switch the police every 60-90 seconds
keyPoints: Eyes up to see the police coming
Protect the ball with the body and the off arm
Low, hard dribble when a police officer is close
Change direction, do not just run faster
variations: U6: police hold a ball too and must dribble
Weak hand only round
U12+: police may steal and keep the ball

drills.name: Ten Passes
drills.description: Possession game with no dribbling. A team scores a point by completing ten passes in a row while the other team tries to steal, deflect or force a bad pass.
instructions: Two teams of 3-6 in a half court, one ball, no baskets used
Offense counts passes out loud, ten consecutive passes equals one point
No dribbling, the ball holder may pivot
A steal, a deflection to the floor or out of bounds gives the ball to the other team and the count restarts
Defense may not grab the ball out of the hands
First team to 3 points wins
keyPoints: Receivers move to open space after passing, no standing
Pass fakes before passes
Catch with two hands and face the ball
Defense pressures the ball and denies the nearest receiver
variations: U6/U8: five passes to score, defender must stay one arm away
Maximum 3 seconds with the ball, same rule as the game block
Every teammate must touch the ball before the point counts
Allow one dribble only to escape a trap

drills.name: Dribble Knockout
drills.description: Everyone dribbles inside a marked area and tries to knock the other balls out while protecting their own. Builds ball protection and awareness in chaos.
instructions: All players dribble inside the three-point arc or the center circle depending on numbers
On the whistle, players knock other balls out of the area while keeping their own dribble
A player whose ball leaves the area or who stops dribbling is out and does 10 pound dribbles on the side
Shrink the area as players are eliminated
Last player dribbling wins
keyPoints: Keep the body between the ball and the nearest opponent
Head up and scan constantly
Low dribble when attacked, higher dribble when free
No pushing or grabbing
variations: Weak hand only
Two-ball version for U12+
Teams: the last team with a player still dribbling wins

drills.name: Sharks and Minnows Dribble
drills.description: Minnows dribble across the court while sharks try to knock their ball away. Caught minnows become sharks. Classic dribbling under pressure game for young groups.
instructions: Minnows line up on one sideline with a ball each, one or two sharks start in the middle without a ball
On the signal, minnows dribble to the opposite sideline
Sharks knock balls away or tag the ball, caught minnows drop their ball and become sharks
Repeat until one minnow remains
keyPoints: Change speed and direction to beat the shark
Eyes up to find the gaps
Protect the ball on the shark's side
Sharks work together to close space
variations: U6: sharks walk only
Minnows must use the weak hand
U10+: sharks also dribble a ball

drills.name: Relay Dribble Races
drills.description: Team relay races down and back using the routine dribble moves, finished with a layup. Adds competition to the end of the warm-up routine.
instructions: Split into 2-4 even teams in lines on the baseline
Coach calls the dribble type: regular, skip, in and out or crossover
First player dribbles to the far basket, makes a layup, dribbles back and hands off
A missed layup must be rebounded and made before returning
First team seated wins the round, change the dribble type each round
keyPoints: Control before speed, a lost ball costs more time than a slower dribble
Layups made, not thrown
Teammates cheer and call the next player
variations: Weak hand round
Add a cone slalom
U12+: finish with a pull-up jumper

drills.name: Red Light Green Light Dribble
drills.description: Coach-controlled stop and go dribbling game for the youngest groups. Teaches dribble control, stopping in balance and reacting to a signal.
instructions: All players have a ball and start on the baseline facing the coach
Green light: dribble forward with the called hand
Red light: jump stop and hold the ball in triple threat
Yellow light: dribble in place, low and hard
Anyone who travels, loses the ball or moves on red goes back three steps
First to reach the coach wins
keyPoints: Jump stop with two feet, knees bent
Triple threat position on every red light
Eyes on the coach, not on the ball
variations: Blue light: switch hands with a crossover
U10+: purple light for a spin or between the legs
Players take turns calling the lights

drills.name: Skill Review Challenge
drills.description: Opening format of the skills block. The skill introduced last session is run again as a short station or point challenge so players recall it before anything new is added.
instructions: Name the skill from last session and ask one player to demonstrate it
Run the skill in 2-3 stations for 3 minutes each, one station per basket or cone group
Score each rep: 1 point for correct technique, 2 points for correct technique at speed
Coach corrects one detail per player, not the whole technique
Finish with a 60-second whole-group challenge using the skill
keyPoints: Review before new content, every session
Players explain the key point in their own words
If fewer than half the group executes correctly, the new skill waits and the review continues
variations: Pair players as coach and athlete, then switch roles
Record the group score and try to beat it next session

drills.name: Triple Threat Introduction
drills.description: Teaches the triple threat stance on the catch: balanced, ball protected at the hip, ready to shoot, pass or drive. First skill of the roadmap for every age group.
instructions: Demonstrate: feet shoulder width, knees bent, ball on the shooting side hip, eyes on the rim
Shadow: players mirror the coach without a ball, then with a ball
Catch into triple threat: partner passes, receiver jump stops and freezes in triple threat for 2 seconds
Add the three options one at a time: shot fake, pass fake, rip through to drive
Add the jab step for U8 and older
Finish with Triple Threat Finishes or 1v1 from Triple Threat
keyPoints: The ball never rests in front of the chest where it can be slapped
The pivot foot stays planted until the drive
Eyes up on the catch to see the defender and the teammates
Fast rip through below the knees
variations: U6: freeze game, coach calls shoot, pass or drive and players shadow the move
U10+: catch on the move coming off a cut
Add a passive defender with the hands up

drills.name: Triple Threat Finishes
drills.description: From a triple threat catch at the wing or elbow, players attack the basket and finish with a different layup each round. Links the stance to scoring.
instructions: Lines at both wings, coach or partner passes to the catch spot
Catch in triple threat, pause one count, then attack
Round 1: direct drive, regular layup with the strong hand
Round 2: crossover drive, layup with the other hand
Round 3: jab step and go
Round 4: free choice of finish: regular, opposite hand, reverse, scoop, or euro step and floater for U12+
The rebounder passes back out to the next player
keyPoints: The first step is long and low, past the imaginary defender's hip
Push the ball out ahead on the first dribble, not beside the body
Finish with the hand away from the defender
Eyes on the target, not on the defender
variations: Add a chair as the defender to drive around
Passive defender who slides but cannot block
Score 2 for a make with the weak hand

drills.name: 1v1 from Triple Threat
drills.description: Competitive application of the triple threat. The attacker receives the ball in triple threat and tries to score against one defender with a dribble limit.
instructions: Attacker at the wing, defender in stance one arm away, coach or the line passes the ball
The attacker must freeze in triple threat for one count before attacking
Maximum 3 dribbles to score: 2 for U6, 4 for U12+
A score is 1 point, a stop gives the defender 1 point
Winner stays for a maximum of 3 rounds, then both rotate
keyPoints: Read the defender's feet and attack the front foot
Use the jab or a fake before the drive
Defender stays low with active hands, no reaching
The one count in triple threat is mandatory
variations: U6: defender keeps the hands behind the back
Start from different spots: top, wing, corner
Team scoring: line versus line

drills.name: Jump Stop and Pivot
drills.description: Teaches stopping in balance with the ball and protecting it with front and reverse pivots. Foundation for the triple threat and for not travelling.
instructions: Players dribble toward a cone and jump stop with both feet landing together
Hold the ball in triple threat for one count
Front pivot 180 degrees on the left foot, then on the right foot
Reverse pivot 180 degrees on each foot
Add a partner who shadows as a defender and tries to touch the ball
Finish with a pass out of the pivot to the next player in line
keyPoints: Both feet land together, knees bent, chest up
The pivot foot heel lifts, the toes stay planted
Ball protected far from the defender with the elbows out
Head up looking for a teammate during the pivot
variations: U6: jump stop on the whistle while dribbling anywhere in the area
Coach calls front or reverse
U10+: pivot and shoot

drills.name: Partner Passing Series
drills.description: Chest, bounce and overhead passes in pairs, stationary then on the move. Standard passing block for the skills section at U6 to U10.
instructions: Pairs 3-4 meters apart: 10 chest passes, 10 bounce passes, 10 overhead passes
Step toward the target on every pass
Receiver shows two hands as a target and calls for the ball
On the move: both players jog the length of the court passing back and forth
Add a third player as a passive defender in the middle for the last round
keyPoints: Thumbs down on the follow-through of the chest pass
The bounce pass lands two thirds of the way to the receiver
Pass to the hands, never above the head for young players
Catch with the eyes on the ball and two hands
variations: U10+: one-hand push pass
Pass on the move to a cutting partner
Count consecutive clean passes and restart at a drop

drills.name: Give and Go
drills.description: The first two-player play of the roadmap: pass, cut hard to the basket and receive the return pass for a layup. Progresses from 2v0 to 2v2.
instructions: Player 1 at the top with the ball, player 2 at the wing
Player 1 passes to the wing and cuts hard to the basket in front of the imaginary defender
Player 2 returns the pass for a layup
Switch roles and sides after each rep
Add one defender on the cutter for 2v1, then a defender on each for 2v2
keyPoints: Cut immediately after the pass, do not watch the ball
Fake away then cut toward the basket
The passer leads the cutter with a bounce or chest pass
Call the name before the return pass
variations: U6: the coach is the wing passer
U10+: backdoor cut if the defender overplays
Finish with a jump stop and shot instead of a layup

drills.name: Defensive Stance and Mirror
drills.description: Introduces the defensive stance and the lateral slide through a mirror game. Players learn to stay low and move their feet before any live 1v1 defense.
instructions: Demonstrate the stance: feet wider than the shoulders, knees bent, back straight, hands active
Slides: sideline to sideline and back without crossing the feet
Mirror: pairs face each other without a ball, the leader moves sideways and the mirror copies for 20 seconds, then switch
Add a ball: the leader dribbles, the mirror slides to stay in front
Live for 10 seconds: the dribbler tries to reach the sideline, the defender stays in front
keyPoints: Stay low, the head stays at the same height while sliding
Push off the trail foot, do not hop
Hands up and active, no reaching for the ball
Nose on the ball for young players
variations: Coach points the directions for the whole group
U10+: zig-zag slides full court
U12+: start the mirror with a closeout

drills.name: Change of Direction Series
drills.description: Crossover, between the legs and behind the back at cones, then against a passive defender. Skills block progression for U10 and older once the warm-up moves are automatic.
instructions: Three cones in a line, 4 meters apart, from the baseline toward the far basket
Round 1: crossover at each cone, finish with a layup
Round 2: between the legs at each cone
Round 3: behind the back at each cone
Round 4: free choice, a partner stands at each cone as a passive defender
Round 5: hesitation then explode past the cone
keyPoints: The change of speed makes the change of direction work
Low and hard on the move dribble
Shoulders go past the cone before the next dribble
Eyes up through every move
variations: U12+: add a retreat dribble before the move
Two-ball version for advanced groups
Race two lines side by side

drills.name: Catch and Shoot Footwork
drills.description: Teaches the 1-2 step and the hop into the shot off a pass. Skills block item for U10 and older once form shooting is stable.
instructions: Shooter at the elbow, passer at the top with the ball
Shooter steps to the ball, catches inside foot then outside foot (1-2 step) and shoots
5 makes, then switch to the hop: both feet land together on the catch
Move to the wing and repeat both footworks
Add a cut from the block to the wing before the catch
keyPoints: Hands ready, shooting hand behind the ball before the catch
Feet pointed at the rim on the landing
Catch low and rise into the shot in one motion
Hold the follow-through
variations: Shot fake and one-dribble pull-up
Competition: first to 10 makes
U12+: add a closeout defender

drills.name: Finishing Package
drills.description: Euro step, floater, power layup and reverse layup from a wing drive. Skills block content for U12 and older, building on the warm-up layup progression.
instructions: Lines at both wings, a cone at the elbow as the help defender
Round 1: euro step around the cone, finish with the outside hand
Round 2: floater over the cone from free throw line distance
Round 3: power layup, two-foot jump stop into the cone, finish strong with two hands
Round 4: reverse layup on the baseline drive
Round 5: live against a help defender who chooses to step up or stay
keyPoints: Decide early, read the help defender before the second dribble
Euro step: long first step one way, second step the other way
Floater: high release, soft wrist, land balanced
Power layup: chin the ball, shoulders square to the basket
variations: Weak hand rounds
Add a trailing defender
Score 2 for a make through contact, coach bumps with a pad

drills.name: 3v0 Pass and Cut
drills.description: Three players learn spacing, pass and cut, and filling the open spot without defense, then against three defenders. Team skill for U10 and older.
instructions: Three players spaced: top, left wing, right wing
The top passes to a wing and cuts to the basket, if no return pass the cutter fills the open wing
The weak side wing replaces to the top
Continue for 30 seconds, then the coach calls shot and the player with the ball scores
Add three defenders playing passive, then live
keyPoints: Pass, cut, fill: nobody stands still
Stay spaced 4-5 meters apart
Cut hard to the rim with the hands ready
Receiver squares up in triple threat on every catch
variations: U8: 2v0 version with the coach as the third player
Live version with a limit of 2 dribbles
Score only off a cut

drills.name: 3v3 Game: 3-Second Possession
drills.description: Regular 3v3 game where each player may keep the ball for a maximum of three seconds. Forces quick decisions, passing and movement. Standard game block rule for U6 to U10.
instructions: Teams of 3, half court for one game, full court when two groups are available
Normal basketball rules adapted to the age group
Each player may hold or dribble the ball for a maximum of 3 seconds, the coach counts out loud
Reaching 3 seconds is a turnover, the defense takes the ball at the top
Scores count normally, play 4-5 minute periods and rotate the teams
keyPoints: Catch in triple threat and decide immediately
Teammates move to get open before the count reaches 2
Coach counts loud and in rhythm, no silent counts
Celebrate good passes as much as scores
variations: U6: 4 seconds for the first weeks
A pass must precede every shot
Make it take it
Add the session's skill as a bonus point

drills.name: Game: Pass Before You Shoot
drills.description: Regular game, 3v3 to 5v5, where a team must complete a minimum number of passes before any shot. Builds patience, spacing and ball movement.
instructions: Set the minimum: 3 passes for U8 and U10, 4 for U12 and older
The coach counts passes out loud, a shot before the minimum is a turnover
A steal or out of bounds resets the count
Fast break layups are allowed only if the team passed at least once in transition
Play normal periods and rotate
keyPoints: Move after passing, a pass to a standing player is a wasted pass
Reverse the ball to the other side at least once
Coach counts loud so players hear the rhythm
variations: Every player must touch the ball before a shot
U12+: only weak hand passes count
A pass that leads to a layup counts double

drills.name: Game: Weak Hand Only
drills.description: Regular game where every dribble and layup must be taken with the weak hand. The strong hand may only pass and catch. Builds the off hand under game pressure.
instructions: Each player declares the weak hand before the game
Any dribble or layup with the strong hand is a turnover
Passing and shooting from distance use the normal technique
Play 3v3 or 4v4 periods of 4 minutes
keyPoints: Protect the ball with the strong hand and the body
Slow down, control before speed
Layup with the weak hand off the correct foot
variations: U8/U10: weak hand dribble only, any hand to finish
Weak hand bonus: a weak hand layup counts 2

drills.name: Game: No Dribble
drills.description: Regular game with no dribbling allowed. Forces passing, cutting, pivoting and spacing. Direct link to the Ten Passes warm-up game.
instructions: No dribbles, a dribble is a turnover
The ball holder may pivot and fake
Receivers must cut or fill open space to get the ball
Normal scoring, 3v3 or 4v4 half court, 4-minute periods
keyPoints: Pivot to protect the ball, do not panic
Cut to the ball or to the rim, no standing
Pass fakes before passes against pressure
variations: Allow one dribble to attack the rim
U6/U8: only bounce passes allowed for one period

drills.name: Game: Skill Bonus Point
drills.description: Regular game in which the skill taught in the skills block earns an extra point every time it is used correctly. Transfers the session's teaching into the game.
instructions: Announce the bonus skill before the game, for example a score from a jab step and go, a layup after a give and go, or a stop with a jump stop
Play the normal rules for the age group
Each correct use of the skill, scored or not, is a bonus point called out by the coach
Review the bonus count at the end of each period
keyPoints: Coach names the skill out loud every time it appears
Players ask what the bonus is before each period
Only one bonus skill per session
variations: Bonus for a defensive skill: stance, slide, closeout
Double bonus if the skill leads directly to a score

drills.name: Game: Layups Only
drills.description: Regular game where only layups count. Forces attacking the rim, cutting and finishing on both sides. For U6 to U10 and for groups that settle for long shots.
instructions: Only layups and shots inside the key count
Any outside shot is a turnover
Normal rules otherwise, 3v3 or 4v4
keyPoints: Attack the rim with the first step
Use the layup progression finishes: regular, opposite hand, reverse
Defense protects the paint, offense passes to the cutter
variations: Weak hand layup counts 2
U10+: reverse layup counts 2
